precepts.text: Honour the physician, but healing itself comes from the Most High.
precepts.point: Asa dies in the one and fortieth year of his reign and is buried in his own sepulchre in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

precepts.why:
“Honour a physician with the honour due unto him for the uses which ye may have of him: for the Lord hath created him. For of the most High cometh healing.”

Asa “was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.” The rebuke is not against physicians. The Lord created the physician, and he is to be honoured. The rebuke is against seeking them in place of the Most High, from whom healing cometh.

precepts.text: In sickness pray to the Most High and leave off from sin, then seek the physician.
precepts.point: Asa dies in the one and fortieth year of his reign and is buried in his own sepulchre in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

precepts.why:
“My son, in thy sickness be not negligent: but pray unto the Lord, and he will make thee whole. Leave off from sin, and order thine hands aright, and cleanse thy heart from all wickedness.”

That is the order: in sickness pray to the Most High and leave off from sin, then seek the physician. Asa did it backwards: “in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.” And “Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.”

points: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: so he had a disease in his feet. Yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians. So who you got to seek first and foremost when you sick? You got to go to the Lord, not the physician first. This brother, he did not go to the Lord; he went to the physicians first.
In the six and thirtieth year of Asa, Baasha king of Israel comes up against Judah and builds Ramah to keep any from going out or coming in to Asa.
Baasha is trying to stop the northern kingdom from coming down to Judah, because tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: Instead of crying to the Most High as he did against Zerah, Asa takes silver and gold out of the house of the Lord and the king's house and hires Benhadad king of Syria to break his league with Baasha.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: Benhadad smites the cities of Israel, so Baasha leaves off building Ramah. Asa carries away the stones and timber of Ramah and builds Geba and Mizpah with them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: Hanani the seer comes to Asa and rebukes him for relying on the king of Syria and not on the Most High, so the host of Syria has escaped his hand. Had he relied on the Most High, he would have delivered them as he did the Ethiopians.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: The eyes of the Most High run to and fro throughout the whole earth to show himself strong for them whose heart is perfect. Asa is wroth, puts the seer in prison, and oppresses some of the people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 16: Asa Leans on Syria Instead of the Most High

points: In the thirty and ninth year of his reign Asa is diseased in his feet, exceeding great, yet he seeks not to the Most High but to the physicians. The rebuke is not against physicians but against seeking them in place of the Most High, from whom healing cometh.
